M-01.note: the validator that runs must be hashed as a bound object, not resolved by name at call time

M-02.note: a tree whose code and registry were rewritten together is self-consistent; only an anchor the mutator does not control can tell it from a legitimate new version

M-05.note: the file is untouched, so only a hash of the object actually bound at runtime can see the transplant

M-06.note: sys.modules must be checked against the hashed surface

M-27.note: the file on disk is untouched, so only checking where the loaded module actually came from can see it

M-28.note: an anchor that can be deleted from the tree it certifies is not an anchor; its absence must stop the system

M-29.note: the trusted key must arrive from outside the tree; a versioned key the mutator may replace anchors nothing

M-31.note: the neutralization is installed before any reference exists, so resolving the validator by name cannot help; the object that runs must itself be hashed
